chunks: "LiPos are dangerous to mishandle because they're a lot of energy in a thin, soft package with a flammable electrolyte, and the damage isn't always visible or immediate.
If you puncture or crush one, or short the terminals, you can get an internal short and thermal runaway, which is fire and toxic smoke.
And a pack can look fine after a drop and ignite later.
For handling: keep terminals insulated, don't carry them loose with metal objects, store them at a partial charge, around 3.
8 volts per cell, in a cool place, ideally in a fire-resistant bag or box. Charge only with the right charger, never unattended, and never charge a swollen or damaged pack.
Don't solder directly to the cell tabs because the heat damages the seal.
For disposal: they can't go in the normal trash or ordinary recycling because in compactors and shredders they get crushed and start fires.
You discharge the pack safely, tape the terminals, and take it to battery recycling or a take-back point.
If it's swollen or damaged, you isolate it in a non-flammable container first. That also recovers cobalt, nickel and lithium instead of landfilling toxic materials."
